messages:
alen: Customer (acct: acme-inc) opened a ticket — their streaming tool_call args are getting truncated on our SSE endpoint, schema validation fails with unexpected EOF. They attached a raw stream capture and a brief trace.

maria: Can you paste the raw SSE capture and the request_id? Also want to know if there's any proxy or CDN in front of us.

alen: Request id: req_20260301_88b7
Raw snippet from the capture (chunks shown with arrows for clarity):

```
event: response
data: {\"type\":\"tool_call\",\"tool\":\"charge\",\"args\":{\"order_id\":\"ord_1234\",\"items\":[{\"id\":\"sku_99\",\"qty\":1}],\"billing\":{\"addr\":\"123 Main\"}
--chunk-boundary--
data: \"shipping\":{\"method\":\"fast\",\"addr\":\"...\"}
--chunk-boundary--
data: \"payment\":{\"token\":\"tok_xyz\"}
--chunk-boundary--
data: }

// final assembled string is missing trailing }} so JSON.parse fails
```

alen: Customer's error: \"invalid_tool_args: Unexpected end of JSON input at position 642\". They only see this when sending arguments > ~1.2KB and only through their EU edge proxy. Direct hits to our hosted endpoint work fine.

josh: Do we have any haproxy/nginx timeouts or chunk coalescing config that could produce a truncated final chunk? Also want to confirm whether the upstream sets `Content-Encoding: gzip` and then a reverse proxy re-streams as chunked transfer. That combo can gap compressed frames.

sophie: I've asked customer for full request headers and TLS termination point. Meanwhile I tried to repro by piping a large SSE payload through our edge mock and a simple node proxy. I could reproduce a truncated trailing brace when the proxy was configured with `proxy_buffering off` and `transfer-encoding: chunked`.

maria: Can you paste the min repro (curl) so infra can run packet captures?

sophie: Repro steps I used: 
```bash
# server: streams a tool_call in SSE with args split across writes
python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 &
# client: emulate proxy that just forwards but breaks on every 512 bytes
node sse-breaker.js --break-size=512 --target=http://localhost:8000/stream
# consumer: curl to see behavior
curl -N http://localhost:9000/stream | sed -n '1,200p'
```
I also attached the tiny Node script that deliberately writes partial JSON across writes. When the middle split happens at a multibyte UTF-8 boundary the downstream sees invalid bytes and some parsers bail early.

ingest-bot: trace:req_20260301_88b7 -> routed through eu-west-1-edge-03 -> backend-host-7. Packet capture id: pcap_20260301_88b7 (attached to internal ticket #INC-559).

josh: Ok assigning to me for a deeper network trace. Hypothesis list: 
1) Edge proxy is re-chunking compressed body incorrectly (gzip midstream) -> truncated inflate on consumer.
2) Keepalive/timeout at proxy causes connection to close mid-SSE and the client library stops reassembling.
3) Our SSE parser expects complete JSON object per event and rejects if final '}' arrives in the same TCP segment but after a pause.

maria: Quick mitigation suggestions to give the customer: 
- Ask them to disable gzip/deflate between their client and the proxy (so proxies don't re-encode).
- Enable exponential backoff and retry of tool_call errors (idempotency key).
- If possible, send arguments in smaller chunks or base64-encode binary to avoid multibyte split issues.

sophie: Customer tried disabling gzip and reported improvement, but still saw occasional `Unexpected end of JSON input`. They're going to run the node repro harness we supplied and forward packet captures.

josh: I'll check haproxy/proxy logs and try reproducing with our real edge config (eu-west-1-edge-03). If I can repro I'll stage a fix to coalesce chunk streams at the proxy before handing to our SSE parser.

alen: Action items:
- josh: capture packets and test with edge config (assigned).
- sophie: collect downstream packet captures and customer repro logs (assigned).
- maria: prepare quick patch to make our SSE argument parser tolerant of trailing pauses (non-blocking failure mode) so we can ship a temporary mitigation.

sophie: customer wants ETA. Can we give 48h for initial findings? :hourglass:

maria: 48h for first pass and a mitigation change if infra can repro. I'll open a PR for a lenient parse mode behind a flag. :thumbsup:

josh: found an entry in haproxy logs showing a `400 client closed connection` 1s after last write — that aligns with proxy cutting connection on idle. I think increasing the proxy write buffer/window or setting `timeout tunnel` might help.

alen: Thanks team. Keeping this thread updated as we get captures. I'll paste customer follow-ups here.

sophie: :white_check_mark: added note to INC-559 with current hypotheses and links to repro scripts.
